about: Every error and warning task game:check finds in the base game, classified: a defect of the game's own files (game-defect), a fault of the committed spec package, with the request sent back to the spec work in docs/decisions.md (spec-package-fault), or a fault of pychivalry to fix (pychivalry-fault, which fails the suite). An entry covers the findings of its code in its file (and layer, game when absent) at each of its lines; a finding with no entry, and an entry line that matches no finding, fail the suite (tools/src/check-suite.ts). Game 1.21.0.3, spec package 1.21.0.3 format 8.

classifications.reason: Not script: sound/GUIDs.txt is a table of sound-bank identifiers, one '{guid} path' per line, which the sound system reads; game:parse leaves it out with that evidence. The spec package lists 'sound' among the game's directories (content type 'sound', source 'snapshot') without saying which of its files are script, and the index reads every .txt file of a listed directory as script, so the parser reports each line. Request to the spec work (docs/decisions.md): mark the files of a listed directory that are not script. A mod shipping its own sound/GUIDs.txt gets the same false findings until then.

Not script: a plain list of model names, one per line, with no '='; game:parse leaves it out with that evidence. The spec package lists 'gfx/models/buildings' among the game's directories (content type 'model_building', source 'snapshot') without saying which of its files are script, and the index reads every .txt file of a listed directory as script. Request to the spec work (docs/decisions.md): mark the files of a listed directory that are not script.

The pattern chinese_grid_pattern_01 is written 'name {' at the top level, without its '='. The rest of the file uses 'name = {'; the catalogue's message names a block name and a body, and the block is read as the pattern's. (As classified for game:parse in tools/data/parse-classifications.json.)

The file ends inside its last event, gdp_visit_holding_decision_event.1507: the event's own closing brace is missing. Counted outside comments and quoted text, the file has 1,399 '{' and 1,398 '}', and its depth is last zero on line 3838. (As classified for game:parse in tools/data/parse-classifications.json.)

A dated entry of a character's history is written '296.1.1 { add_spouse = ... }', without its '='; every other entry has one. The same defect that release 2.3.0 recorded in history/characters/japanese.txt on game 1.20, which 1.21.0.3 no longer has. (As classified for game:parse in tools/data/parse-classifications.json.)

'filter' is written directly inside any_vassal, in a trigger_if of the decision's is_valid. 'filter' is no trigger of the game's documentation (triggers.log, 1.21.0.3), and the game's documentation of its list iterators gives 'filter =' only to the in_de_jure_hierarchy iterators; the spec package's iterator_params entry for 'filter' (confirmed) lists only that list and records this one use inside any_vassal as undocumented. Inside any_vassal the key is read as a trigger, which the game does not have.

'save_scope_as = liege_temp' is written in the limit of an if in try_to_set_event_recurrer_relationship_effect: a trigger block. save_scope_as is an effect only in the game's documentation (the package's buckets: effects); the trigger that saves a scope is save_temporary_scope_as (triggers and effects).

'is_powerful = yes' in get_potential_enemies_effect: is_powerful is no trigger of game 1.21.0.3's documentation, nor a name the base game defines, nor in the package's removed list. The trigger the base game uses for a powerful vassal is is_powerful_vassal (260 uses).

'is_powerful = yes' beside is_vassal_of: is_powerful is no trigger of game 1.21.0.3's documentation, nor a name the base game defines, nor in the package's removed list. The trigger the base game uses for a powerful vassal is is_powerful_vassal (260 uses).

can_elevate_holy_site and can_demote_holy_site, in the limits of elevate_holy_site_effect and demote_holy_site_effect: neither is a trigger of game 1.21.0.3's documentation, a name the base game defines, or in the package's removed list. Neither scripted effect is called anywhere in the base game.

elevate_holy_site and demote_holy_site: neither is an effect of game 1.21.0.3's documentation, a name the base game defines, or in the package's removed list (which says holy sites are now created and removed: create_holy_site, remove_holy_site, add_holy_site, make_holy_site_eminent). Neither enclosing scripted effect is called anywhere in the base game.

secret_is_blackmailable_trigger calls secret_is_blackmailable_strong_hook_trigger and secret_is_blackmailable_weak_hook_trigger, which no file of the base game defines and the game does not document; secret_is_blackmailable_trigger itself is called nowhere in the base game.

'selection_count = 1' directly inside every_top_trade_good_in_range. The game's own documentation of its list iterators gives selection_count to the top_trade_good_in_range iterators: the spec package's iterator_params entry for selection_count says so in its own script_docs evidence (bases_found: desired_tenet, top_trade_good_in_range, undesired_tenet), but the entry (confirmed) lists only desired_tenet and undesired_tenet, which the reader takes as written. Request to the spec work (docs/decisions.md): add top_trade_good_in_range to the entry's lists.
